findings.title: Cleanup ticker cut from 10 minutes to 1 minute, so every background cleanup job now runs ten times as often
findings.description: `Run` changes `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.Minute * 1`. Each tick calls `clean` (cleanup.go:88-121), which runs all eight jobs: temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, and query history. The query-history job runs two row-limit enforcement queries. Every one of these now runs every minute instead of every ten. The 9-minute timeout in `clean` is unchanged, and nothing in the diff explains the cadence change. On a busy instance this is about ten times the background DELETE and scan load, and it also makes the annotation cleanup from the next finding run every minute. If this was a debugging aid, it should be reverted before merge.

findings.title: Every annotation and tag cleanup batch is logged at ERROR level, including runs that delete nothing
findings.description: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579 log each batch at `Error` level. The first line in each pair also logs the full `ids` slice. These calls run even when nothing matches: `fetchIDs` returns an empty slice, and the "cleaned" line still logs `count=0` at Error. `CleanAnnotations` runs once per configured retention rule, so an instance with any max-age or max-count retention set emits about two ERROR lines per rule on every run, even when idle. With the 1-minute ticker from the previous finding, that is about two ERROR lines per minute per rule. The `err` field on the first line is always nil at that point. Operators who alert on error-level logs will be paged for routine, successful cleanup. Progress should be logged at Debug or Info, and Error should be reserved for actual failures.

findings.title: Batch DELETE binds one parameter per ID on MySQL and Postgres, so a batch size above their bind-parameter limit makes cleanup fail
findings.description:
`deleteByIDs` builds `DELETE FROM <table> WHERE id IN (?,?,...)` with one placeholder per ID. The count is bounded only by `cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`, which `setting.go:710` reads as an unbounded `int64` with default 100. The only escape hatch is the SQLite branch at line 608, which inlines the IDs. Grafana's MySQL DSN (`sqlstore.go:287`) does not set `interpolateParams`, so the driver uses server-side prepared statements, which allow at most 65535 placeholders. Postgres has the same 65535 bind-parameter limit at the protocol level.

If an operator sets the batch size above 65535 and one batch matches at least 65536 rows, the DELETE returns an error. `untilDoneOrCancelled` propagates it, and `cleanUpOldAnnotations` (cleanup.go:126-127) logs it. The fetch returns the same top-of-list batch on every run, so cleanup gets stuck there on every run. The previous single-statement DELETE used no bind parameters, so this configuration worked before the change. The default batch size does not trigger it.
